instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor conducting a reassessment. Analyse the prior assessment summary, changes since last assessment, and updated survey, then respond with a complete reassessment JSON including score_delta, carry_forward, progress, and comparison_to_previous.

answers.companyDescription: Private hospital group operating 3 general hospitals and 8 outpatient clinics with 450 beds and 1,800 staff including 350 physicians. Performing 22,000 surgeries annually. Currently implementing an integrated hospital information system and evaluating AI-assisted radiology image triage for chest X-rays and CT scans. The organization has significant capital, talent depth, and existing technology infrastructure, but internal processes are designed for stability and risk management — not speed. Innovation initiatives must navigate procurement, legal, compliance, and IT security review before receiving green-light. The key challenge is not resource availability but organizational velocity.
answers.pastInitiatives: We have a mature innovation program with a dedicated R&D lab of 12 engineers, an annual innovation budget equivalent to 5% of revenue, and a structured stage-gate process for evaluating and funding new initiatives. In the past 3 years we have launched 4 new product lines that now contribute 18% of total revenue, including an AI-powered recommendation engine that has become our fastest-growing SKU.
answers.strategicGoals: We are heavily dependent on a single product category and a concentrated customer base — our top 3 clients represent 55% of revenue. This concentration risk is unacceptable for our long-term health. We need to identify and develop new revenue streams, possibly including new product lines for different customer segments or entirely new business models that leverage our existing capabilities.
answers.teamSize: Our digital and innovation organization includes 80+ professionals across centers of excellence for AI/ML, cloud engineering, UX design, and agile delivery. We run an internal incubator program that has graduated 6 new digital products to market in the past 2 years, alongside a corporate venture capital arm that makes strategic minority investments in relevant startups.

input.changes_since_last: Hired 7 new team members. Launched customer feedback pilot. Budget for innovation increased 20%.

opportunities.title: Streamline Innovation Review Cycle (Fast-Track Sandboxing)
opportunities.rationale: The primary bottleneck is not resource availability but the organizational velocity within the review process. Establishing a dedicated, compliance-vetted fast track for minor initiatives will allow faster market testing without fully abandoning rigorous risk management required by the sector. This addresses the tension between stability and speed.

first_actions: Establish an interdepartmental 'Fast Track' review committee involving legal, compliance, and IT security representatives to define scope and exclusion criteria.
Pilot a sandbox environment for 1-2 non-critical digital features from the existing incubator portfolio.
Develop clear Service Level Agreements (SLAs) defining the maximum time allowed for initial concept vetting.
execution_plan.success_metric: Average time to approve a pilot feature reduced by 40%
milestones: Formal integration into the Stage-Gate process (H2)

opportunities.title: Develop New Revenue Streams via Adjacent Market Expansion
opportunities.rationale: The current concentration risk (top 3 clients = 55% revenue) is a critical threat to long-term stability. Leveraging existing capabilities (AI/ML, patient data insights) into adjacent care models or non-hospital segments will diversify the revenue base and mitigate client dependency. This directly addresses strategic diversification.

first_actions: Conduct deep market analysis identifying 3 high-potential, low-barrier adjacent service lines (e.g., remote monitoring for specific chronic care groups).
Develop a financial model projecting revenue growth from diversifying into the top 2 identified markets.
Incorporate legal and regulatory requirements for new geographic or patient demographics into the concept phase.
execution_plan.success_metric: Pipeline identified with 2 viable, diversified revenue models achieving $XM potential within 3 years.

next_steps.action: Formalize the governance structure and compliance checkpoints for the 'Fast Track' sandbox concept to ensure legal and regulatory adherence.
Host a strategic workshop involving the C-suite, R&D leads, and BD team to map core technological capabilities against high-growth, non-hospitality markets.

Review and update the internal KPI tracking system to include metrics related to organizational velocity (e.g., cycle time reduction, number of pilots launched per quarter) alongside financial outcomes.

key_weaknesses: Organizational friction/lack of velocity: Processes are optimized for stability and risk management, creating significant drag on speed-to-market.
High revenue concentration risk: Over-reliance on the top three clients (55% of revenue) poses a systemic threat to diversification goals.
Dependency on formal gating processes: While robust, the stage-gate process acts as a bottleneck when rapid iteration or pivoting is required.

improvements: Significant increase in innovation budget (20%) and talent depth (7 new hires).
Formal launch of customer feedback collection (NPS) provides actionable data.
Maturation of internal capabilities, evidenced by 6 products graduating from the incubator program.
persistent_gaps: The core challenge remains organizational velocity—the speed of decision-making and operational change is not keeping pace with resource investment.
Strategic diversification efforts need to move beyond identifying opportunities into concrete, de-risked business models.
Integration of new process tools needs to be systematically phased to avoid further disruption.
achieved_milestones: Completed stage 3 review for previous recommendations (allowing next steps to begin).
Established a dedicated R&D lab and structured stage-gate process, confirming commitment to innovation maturity.
Successfully piloted customer feedback mechanisms via NPS surveys.

comparison_to_previous.key_changes: Improved funding (increased budget by 20%), increased human capital (7 new hires), and formalized customer feedback loops. The organization has transitioned from merely planning for innovation to actively building the capability infrastructure.
